'''Christine Silberhorn''' (born 19 April 1974) is a German physicist specialising in [[quantum optics]] and a full professor at the [[Paderborn University]]. In 2011, Silberhorn was awarded the [[Leibniz Prize]] and was the youngest recipient of the 2.5 million Euro prize at that time.<ref name=":0" />

== Education ==

Born in [[Nürnberg]], Germany, Silberhorn studied mathematics and [[physics]] at [[Erlangen University]] (1993–1999) and completed her Ph.D. in 2003, with a dissertation in [[quantum information science]]. She did postdoctoral work at [[Clarendon Laboratory]] of [[Oxford University]] and was a Junior Research Fellow of [[Wolfson College, Oxford|Wolfson College]] in Oxford in 2003–2004.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae Prof. Dr. Christine Silberhorn|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Silberhorn_Christine_D.pdf|website=www.leopoldina.org|access-date=10 May 2020|archive-date=26 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190526162151/https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/redaktion/Mitglieder/CV_Silberhorn_Christine_D.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>  In 2005 she joined the Max Planck Research Group "Optics, Information and Photonics" (now the [[Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light]]) as the head of the junior research group "integrated quantum optics".

== Career ==
In 2005, Silberhorn joined the Erlangen branch of the [[Max Planck Institute for Quantum Optics]] Garching, heading the Junior Research Group Integrated Quantum Optics until 2008. Upon foundation of the [[Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light]] Erlangen, she headed the Integrated Quantum Optics Group until 2010, completing her [[habilitation]] in 2008. Silberhorn is currently Chair for Integrated Quantum Optics at [[Paderborn University]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://physik.uni-paderborn.de/en/silberhorn/ |title=University web site of Silberhorn group |author=<!--Not stated--> |access-date=14 March 2019 |archive-date=6 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180906200223/https://physik.uni-paderborn.de/en/silberhorn/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Research ==
Silberhorn's research is dedicated to novel optical technologies based on [[quantum optics]], and light-based quantum systems for use in [[quantum communication]] and [[quantum information processing]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://idw-online.de/de/news667515|title=Forschergruppe der Uni Paderborn entwickelt neuen Ansatz für die Quantenkommunikation|website=idw-online.de|access-date=13 May 2019|archive-date=13 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190513090137/https://idw-online.de/de/news667515|url-status=live}}</ref>

She has contributed to the development of engineered quantum light sources using [[Integrated quantum photonics|integrated optics]] and ultrafast pulsed lasers, the implementation of multichannel [[quantum networks]] for photon counting and [[quantum simulator|quantum simulations]], and the realization of [[quantum communication]] systems with bright light.

Silberhorn is best known for her role in leading a research project which developed photon translators for use in [[quantum computing]] and [[Quantum information science|quantum communication]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Chen|first=Sophia|date=15 November 2019|title=Quantum computers can talk to each other via a photon translator|url=https://newscientist.com/article/2112801-quantum-computers-can-talk-to-each-other-via-a-photon-translator/|journal=New Scientist}}</ref> In 2016, the team that she ran jointly with professor [[Thomas Zentgraf]] was awarded the largest [[European Research Council]] grant for their research.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nw.de/lokal/kreis_paderborn/paderborn/paderborn/21515701_Millionen-Foerderung-fuer-Physiker-der-Uni-Paderborn.html|title=Millionen-Förderung für Physiker der Uni Paderborn|date=17 December 2016|website=Neue Westfälische|language=de|access-date=13 May 2019}}</ref> In 2019, Silberhorn's team demonstrated the [[Hong–Ou–Mandel effect|Hong–Ou–Mandel experiment]] on a single integrated photonic chip by creating, bunching and detecting two individual photons and integrating components of quantum photonics on a single chip.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.owl-journal.de/neuartiger-schaltkreis-fuer-die-quantenphotonik-entwickelt/|title=Neuartiger Schaltkreis für die Quantenphotonik entwickelt|last=VMS|date=17 January 2019|website=OWL == Awards ==
Silberhorn's research on the quantum properties of light and the development of quantum devices has received worldwide recognition and numerous awards, including the [[Hertha Sponer Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dpg-physik.de/vereinigungen/fachuebergreifend/ak/akc/sponerpreis/preistraegerinnen-der-vergangenen-jahre|title=Herta Sponer Prize Awardees|access-date=14 March 2019|language=de|archive-date=28 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200928224645/https://www.dpg-physik.de/vereinigungen/fachuebergreifend/ak/akc/sponerpreis/preistraegerinnen-der-vergangenen-jahre|url-status=live}}</ref> of the [[German Physical Society]] and the Medal of the [[Werner von Siemens Ring]] Foundation in 2007,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://siemens-ring.de/dr-christine-silberhorn/|title=Werner von Siemens Ring Foundation|date=18 January 2016|access-date=14 March 2019|language=de|archive-date=8 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200808110913/https://siemens-ring.de/dr-christine-silberhorn/|url-status=live}}</ref> the [[Heinz Maier-Leibnitz-Preis]] in 2008 and the [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz-Prize]] in 2011.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.dfg.de/en/funded_projects/prizewinners/leibniz_prize/2011/silberhorn/index.html|title=Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft|website=Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize Laudatio|access-date=14 March 2019|archive-date=24 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130624210726/http://www.dfg.de/en/funded_projects/prizewinners/leibniz_prize/2011/silberhorn/index.html}}</ref> For the latter, she was the youngest scientist to receive this award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fau.de/2011/01/alumni/interviews/prof-dr-christine-silberhorn/|title=Quantenphysikerin im Interview|date=7 January 2011|website=Friedrich-Alexander Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg|access-date=13 May 2019|archive-date=13 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190513090151/https://www.fau.de/2011/01/alumni/interviews/prof-dr-christine-silberhorn/}}</ref> In 2019, Silberhorn was named a Fellow of [[The Optical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=18 October 2018|title=The Optical Society Announces 2019 Fellows Class|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/newsroom/news_releases/2018/the_optical_society_announces_2019_fellows_class/|access-date=28 October 2020|website=The Optical Society|archive-date=26 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200926030446/https://www.osa.org/en-us/about_osa/newsroom/news_releases/2018/the_optical_society_announces_2019_fellows_class/|url-status=live}}</ref>

She has been a member of [[Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|Leopoldina]], the national academy of Germany, since 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/member/7558/|title=Leopoldina Membership Card|website=Leopoldina|access-date=14 March 2019|archive-date=28 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141228183857/http://www.leopoldina.org/en/members/list-of-members/member/7558/|url-status=live}}</ref>
